header:
Date: 2027-09-02 UTC | Start: 14:00 | Duration: 52m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Samantha Lee (Aurora Head of ML), Dr. Raj Patel (Aurora Data Dir), Emily Carter (Aurora Security), Jamal Ortiz (Aurora Eng).
Recording: Fireflies.ai auto-transcript (medium quality)
summary: POC scoping focused on open-model selection for Aurora Health's clinical summarization use case. Discussed success criteria (fidelity, hallucination rate, latency under 350ms p95 for short prompts), workload sizing (peak 300 qps, 20M tokens/day), benchmark plan, timelines for a 6-week POC, data security requirements (KMS, VPC/private deployment), and a short list of open models to evaluate (Llama 3-Chat, Mistral X, RedPanda-2, Falcon Instruct variants). Next steps: Redwood to send benchmark harness and recommended config; Aurora to provide sample data and security checklist.
topics: Workload sizing: qps, tokens/day, avg prompt/response length
Benchmarks: evaluation metrics and test harness
Model shortlist: open models, quantization, domain adaptation
Security: SOC2, KMS, VPC/private options, data residency
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm maya from Redwood, we got Diego on the line, and Auroras team, wanna do quick intros.
[00:12] Samantha: yeah hi i'm samantha, head of ml at aurora health.
[00:15] Raj: raj here, director of data.
[00:18] Emily: emily, security.
[00:20] Diego: quick agenda—success criteria, workload sizing, pick models, benchmark plan, timelines. sound good?
[00:27] Samantha: yep, that's what we need. to start, our main thing is clinical note summarization and triage. accuracy and hallucinations are top priority, latency is second but still important for provider workflow.
[00:40] Raj: to add numbers, peak expected concurrent qps around 250-300 during shifts, avg prompt length 150 tokens, avg response 200 tokens, around 18-22M tokens per day.
[00:53] Jamal: environment is AWS us-east-1, we have strict PII rules, need KMS integration and audit logs. might consider VPC/private deployment for the pilot if needed.
[01:05] Maya: got it. just to align on success criteria—would you say: 1) factual accuracy/hallucination rate below x% on our eval set, 2) clinician acceptability 90% on sampled reviews, 3) latency p95 under 350ms for short prompts, and 4) cost target under $Y per 1k responses?
[01:26] Samantha: that sounds right, replace x% with a target we can iterate on—start with <5% hallucination for critical fields. cost target will depend on model options, but lower is better.
[01:36] Diego: for benchmarking we'll run three tiers—small context tests (short notes), long context (full visit transcripts), and safety/regression tests with red-teaming prompts. we'll measure rouge/entailment/hallucination metrics plus latency and tokens/sec.
[01:50] Raj: question—open models can vary a lot for medical domain; do you have a recommended shortlist?
[01:56] Diego: yep, based on prior pilots and perf profiles we recommend starting with 4 variants: Llama-3-chat 16B (fp16 & q4 variants), Mistral X-instruct 8/12B, Falcon-180B-Instruct quantized, and RedPanda-2-13B (a community tuned model we saw good clinical behaviour on). also include a smaller distilled model as a cheap baseline.
[02:21] Samantha: any concerns about hallucinations with those open models?
[02:24] Diego: yeah tradeoffs—larger models like Falcon or Llama 3 tend to be better on factuality but cost more; some community-tuned smaller models show decent precision on common templates but fail on edge cases. we should include calibration steps and a safety filter. also quantization can slightly impact factuality, so we'll test q4 vs fp16.
[02:42] Emily: from security perspective we need to know whether data leaves our VPC and how keys are handled. can Redwood run the pilot in our VPC?
[02:50] Maya: we offer hosted API for fastest start, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private (VPC/on-prem). for pilots we commonly start hosted for speed then move to Dedicated or Private if audit requires. Private supports customer-managed KMS and full audit logs.
[03:06] Emily: do you have SOC2 and iso certs?
[03:09] Maya: yes SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001, i'll attach certs and our security pack. we'll also include KMS integration notes.
[03:16] Jamal: rough timeline? we want a pilot in about 6 weeks.
[03:19] Diego: suggested schedule—week 1: benchmark plan + data ingest, week 2: baseline run on hosted models, weeks 3-4: tuning and rerun with quantized variants, week 5: user sampling and clinician review, week 6: wrap + decision. if we need private deployment that'll add provisioning time (~2 weeks).
[03:39] Samantha: sounds doable. what about evaluation metrics—how do you measure hallucinations?
[03:44] Diego: we'll use a combined approach—automatic entailment checks (NLI), factuality scores, and human review on a stratified sample. we'll produce confusion tables and per-field recall/precision for critical entities.
[03:56] Raj: any specific infra notes—GPU types, batching, latency expectations?
[03:59] Diego: for hosted we've profiled on A100 and H100 class nodes; typical p95 for 16B q4 models is around 120-220ms with micro-batching tuned, larger 70-180B models hit 300-500ms depending on quantization and seq length. continuous batching and KV cache improvements help overall throughput. if you need strict p95 <350ms we can recommend model/quantization combos.
[04:26] Samantha: can you give a recommended starting pair—one accuracy-focused, one cost-focused?
[04:30] Diego: accuracy: Llama-3-chat-16B fp16 or q4 if you need cost/throughput tradeoff; cost-focused: RedPanda-2-13B quantized or a distilled Mistral variant. include Falcon-180B as an upper-bound for quality.
[04:46] Emily: on data residency, we need logs retained 1 year, and ability to purge data on demand. is that supported?
[04:52] Maya: yes retention policies configurable; we support on-request purge and audit logs. Private deployment gives the most control.
[04:59] Jamal: we'll share sample dataset—5k de-identified notes, and also a small eval set of 500 labeled summaries.
[05:05] Samantha: and clinician review—we'll provide 20 clinician reviewers for sampling in week 5.
[05:09] Diego: great, for benchmarks i'll include latency profiles by model and quantization (fp16, q4, q8_0), and a cost per 1k responses estimate. we'll also include a simple safety filter pipeline you can run client-side.
[05:24] Raj: curious about fallbacks—if a cheaper model fails, can we route to a higher-tier model automatically?
[05:29] Maya: yes, smart routing and automatic fallback is part of Redwood—policy-based routing by latency/cost/region, with automatic degradation to cached responses or higher model when needed.
[05:38] Emily: any red flags for compliance—do you do data residency per request?
[05:41] Diego: we can pin routing to region and do per-customer tenancy. for strict customers we recommend Private.
[05:47] Samantha: ok last bit—what do you need from us right now?
[05:50] Maya: sample data, redaction rules, success metric thresholds, and confirmation on whether you want hosted-first or private-first pilot. we'll send benchmark harness and security docs.
[06:00] Samantha: we'll aim to upload samples by sept 6 and prefer hosted-first to move faster, but may request private later.
[06:06] Maya: perfect—recap and action items we'll email after the call. thanks all.
[06:10] Emily: thanks.
[06:12] End of recording (approx 52 minutes).
